cs.t: - Buy an LG OLED TV. They're as gorgeous as they are notorious. I just got a 77" LG C6 and it is crazy good. - Root it [0]. - Install Glasshouse [1] and disable all telemetry.  YOU  now own the glass. Now you can chromecast to the TV, use Adfree YouTube, access IP TV, etc etc etc. No point crippling your TV by pulling the wireless module and voiding your warranty. - Install a bunch of cool apps to your TV [2] (there are many more out there besides those listed here) - Restore to Factory Defaults if you ever want / need to unroot and get back to stock e.g. a warranty claim The  only  issue is that LG recently closed the vulnerability that made rooting possible so you  don't  want any firmware released after 2026-10-10 like 43.21.84. Hopefully a new exploit is found that makes rooting possible once again. BTW, you might have heard of Dev Mode on these TVs but they don't allow anywhere near the functionality that rooting provides. [0]  https://tv.slada.sk/guides/rooting-guide  [1]  https://github.com/rorygallagher2024/glasshouse  [2]  https://www.webosbrew.org/
cs.th: Ask HN: Which TV do you recommend for privacy?

cs.t: I do actually have this setup going with a Cable Matters adapter [1] + a custom firmware I found [2] and > chroma/RGB 4:4:4 + HDR + VRR/Freesync + 4k,120hz for their Linux PC on a TV works great now on my LG C4 TV with Bazzite's gaming mode, though: * 144Hz is unstable * 12-bit color is unstable (10-bit works fine), and gamescope doesn't have a way to limit color depth (kwin does), so I had to put in place an EDID override * in the EDID, limiting the FreeSync range to 60-120Hz (which should still allow frame doubling/tripling) seemed to be better -- the default 40Hz caused a bit of flickering because the AMD driver would drop the refresh rate down to 38.5Hz or so. Should write about this in more detail. [1]  https://www.amazon.com/dp/B094XR43M5  [2]  https://forum.level1techs.com/t/it-is-possible-to-4k-120-hdr...
